gates.title: AND
gates.lesson: An AND gate only outputs 1 when every input is 1.

gates.title: OR
gates.lesson: OR is inclusive: both inputs at 1 still produce 1.

gates.title: NOT
gates.lesson: The small output bubble means inversion. NOT has exactly one input.

gates.title: NAND
gates.lesson: NAND is universal: combinations of NAND gates can implement any Boolean function.

gates.title: NOR
gates.lesson: NOR is universal. Its output is 1 only when all inputs are 0.

gates.title: XOR
gates.description: An odd number of inputs is 1.
gates.lesson: For two inputs XOR means different. With 3 or 4 inputs, it means ODD parity—not exactly one 1.

gates.title: XNOR
gates.description: An even number of inputs is 1.
gates.lesson: For two inputs XNOR means equal. With 3 or 4 inputs, it means EVEN parity—not that all inputs are equal.

gates.title: BUFFER
gates.lesson: A buffer has one input. It preserves the logic value; electrical drive strength is not modeled.

circuits.title: Half adder
lesson: Adds two one-bit values. It has no carry-in.
Read Carry:Sum as a two-bit number; 1 + 1 = 10₂, not a single output of 2.

circuits.title: Full adder
lesson: Includes a carry-in, so three one-bit values are added.
Cout:Sum represents A + B + Cin. Connect Cout to the next stage’s Cin for a ripple adder.

circuits.title: Half subtractor
lesson: Subtracts B from A. Operand order matters.
When A=0 and B=1, Diff=1 with Borrow=1. This is binary subtraction, not an ordinary negative output bit.

circuits.title: Full subtractor
lesson: Computes A − B − Bin.
Bout indicates that the next higher stage must supply a borrow; Diff = (A − B − Bin) mod 2.

circuits.title: 2:1 multiplexer
lesson: A multiplexer selects one data input, not one output.
S=0 selects D0; S=1 selects D1. Changing an unselected input does not affect Y.

circuits.title: 4:1 multiplexer
lesson: S1 is the most significant select bit. 00/01/10/11 select D0/D1/D2/D3.
There are six independent inputs, so the full truth table has 64 rows.

circuits.title: 1:2 demultiplexer
lesson: Routes one data input to one selected output.
The unselected output is 0. It is not a multiplexer with reversed labels.

circuits.title: 2:4 decoder + enable
lesson: Active-high one-hot outputs. A is the MSB.
When disabled no output is asserted; this differs from a decoder without an enable input.

circuits.title: 4:2 priority encoder
lesson: Unlike a basic one-hot encoder, multiple active inputs are allowed: the highest index wins.
Valid distinguishes D0=1 (code 00) from no active input (code 00, Valid=0).

circuits.title: 1-bit magnitude comparator
lesson: Compares unsigned one-bit values.
Exactly one of LT/EQ/GT is 1 for every valid input.

circuits.title: 2-bit magnitude comparator
formula: If equal, compare A0 vs B0
lesson: Unsigned values A=2A1+A0 and B=2B1+B0.
The least-significant comparison only matters when the most-significant bits match.

circuits.title: 4-bit ripple-carry adder
lesson: Four full-adder stages carry from bit 0 toward bit 3.
A3/B3 are the MSBs. S3…S0 is the low four-bit sum; Cout is the fifth bit.
This ideal model has no propagation-delay simulation. The 512-row truth table is paginated.

circuits.title: 8:1 multiplexer
formula: Y = D[base-2 index selected by S2, S1, S0]
lesson: 3 select bits choose exactly one of 8 data inputs.
Select inputs are ordered most-significant first; 0… selects D0…D7.
A full table has 2^11 rows and is paginated on demand.

circuits.title: 16:1 multiplexer
formula: Y = D[base-2 index selected by S3, S2, S1, S0]
lesson: 4 select bits choose exactly one of 16 data inputs.
Select inputs are ordered most-significant first; 0… selects D0…D15.
A full table has 2^20 rows and is paginated on demand.

circuits.title: 1:4 demultiplexer
lesson: Routes one data input to the output selected by the binary select word.
Select inputs are most-significant first. With D=0 every output is 0.
A full table has 2^3 rows and is paginated on demand.

circuits.title: 1:8 demultiplexer
formula: Y[i] = D when select = i; all other outputs are 0.
lesson: Routes one data input to the output selected by the binary select word.
Select inputs are most-significant first. With D=0 every output is 0.
A full table has 2^4 rows and is paginated on demand.

circuits.title: 1:16 demultiplexer
formula: Y[i] = D when select = i; all other outputs are 0.
lesson: Routes one data input to the output selected by the binary select word.
Select inputs are most-significant first. With D=0 every output is 0.
A full table has 2^5 rows and is paginated on demand.

circuits.title: 3:8 decoder
formula: Y[i] = 1 exactly when input A = i (0…7).
lesson: Active-high one-hot outputs; exactly one output is 1 for every input word.
Input A2 is the most significant bit.

circuits.title: 4:16 decoder
formula: Y[i] = 1 exactly when input A = i (0…15).
lesson: Active-high one-hot outputs; exactly one output is 1 for every input word.
Input A3 is the most significant bit.

circuits.title: 4-bit magnitude comparator
formula: LT is true at the first (most-significant) bit where A=0 and B=1.
Exactly one of LT, EQ or GT is 1.
lesson: Unsigned words A=A3A2A1A0 and B=B3B2B1B0 are compared lexicographically from the MSB.
A lower bit matters only when every more-significant bit is equal.

circuits.title: 3-bit even-parity generator
lesson: Append P to the three data bits.
P is 1 when the data contain an odd number of 1s, making the total number of 1s even.

circuits.title: 4-bit even-parity checker
lesson: Even=1 means the received four-bit word has even parity.
Error=1 means an odd number of 1s was received; this detects, but cannot correct, an odd-bit error.

circuits.title: BCD-to-seven-segment decoder
formula: A B C D are 8-4-2-1 BCD inputs.
a…g are active-high segments for a common-cathode display.
lesson: Digits 0–9 display their decimal glyph; invalid BCD inputs 10–15 turn every segment off.
The model describes logic only; it does not model current limiting, display wiring or physical polarity.

sequential.title: SR latch · NOR
lesson: Active-high, level-sensitive, cross-coupled NOR gates.
During S=R=1, both physical outputs are 0. Releasing to 00 leaves memory indeterminate until a valid set/reset.

sequential.title: SR latch · NAND
lesson: Inputs nS/nR are active-low. A leading n means inversion.
During nS=nR=0 both physical outputs are 1; after release the stored state is indeterminate.

sequential.title: D latch · enable
sequential.rule: EN=1: Q follows D · EN=0: hold
lesson: A transparent latch is NOT an edge-triggered flip-flop.
While EN is high, changing D changes Q immediately. Lower EN to hold the last value.

sequential.title: D flip-flop
lesson: A rising-edge flip-flop samples only a 0→1 clock edge.
Changing D while CLK remains high does not update Q. Falling edges do not capture D.

sequential.title: SR flip-flop
lesson: The SR inputs are sampled on rising edges, not continuously.
S=R=1 at a rising edge is forbidden; use a valid set/reset to recover.

sequential.title: JK flip-flop
lesson: JK allows the 11 case: it toggles the stored bit.
Q(next) = JQ′ + K′Q on a rising edge. This ideal edge model does not simulate race-around.

sequential.title: T flip-flop
lesson: Q(next) = T ⊕ Q on a rising edge.
Holding CLK high does not repeatedly toggle Q.

sequential.title: 3-bit up counter
sequential.rule: On ↑CLK: RESET wins; EN counts mod 8
lesson: Synchronous active-high RESET takes effect only at a rising edge.
EN=0 holds the count. After 111 the count wraps to 000.

sequential.title: 4-bit shift register
sequential.rule: On ↑CLK: RESET wins; EN shifts D into Q0
lesson: Shift direction is toward Q3: Q3←Q2←Q1←Q0←D.
The earliest serial bit moves toward the MSB. RESET is synchronous, not asynchronous.

sequential.title: 4-bit ring counter
lesson: This demonstration starts and resets one-hot. A real all-zero ring cannot start without initialization.

sequential.title: 4-bit Johnson counter
sequential.rule: On ↑CLK: shift inverted Q3 into Q0
lesson: The four-bit twisted-ring counter has eight states in its initialized cycle. RESET is synchronous.
